name: fade-in
description: What loads in fades in: elements inserted while a page is loading, and images when their pixels arrive, appear over 450ms instead of popping in. A utility class plus a small observer; no markup of its own.

props.name: content
props.default: Content that arrived after the page was drawn.
props.description: Template only: the text of the sample element. In use, the class .ds-fade-in goes on any element, or component.js adds it.

props.name: hold
props.description: data-fade-hold on an element in the page's HTML: it stays invisible and nothing inserted inside it fades on its own until dsFadeIn.settle() (or the 10s fail-safe); then it fades in once, as a whole.

props.name: region
props.description: data-fade-region on the area under the page's nav bar: dsFadeIn.leave(url) fades it out (200ms) before going to url.

rationale: A page that fills tables and sidebars from an API used to show a veil and hide everything until the data was in. Now nothing is hidden: the static page is drawn at once and each element that arrives fades in (opacity 0 to 1 with a 4px rise, 450ms ease-out, staggered 18ms per item up to 360ms). component.js watches insertions until the page calls dsFadeIn.settle() (or 10s pass), fades the topmost inserted element of each batch, and holds an image that is still downloading invisible until it has loaded, so a thumbnail fades in when it arrives, also after settle. After settle a re-render (sort, filter) is not animated: only what was loading fades. The fill mode is backwards, not both, so the finished fade leaves no stacking context behind. Not sourced from Figma (explicit request 2026-10-12, replacing the page-level loading state). Under prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Hold (explicit request 2026-10-24, "content appears once, with the animation"): on a page whose first view takes several requests (a list, then the item, then a preview), element-by-element fading showed the view in waves: skeletons, then each part as it arrived, then late pictures. A host marks its main area data-fade-hold; it is opacity 0, inner insertions are not animated, and settle() removes the attribute and fades the area in as one piece, so the host calls settle() when the last part is drawn. The fail-safe still releases it after 10s. Leave (explicit request 2026-10-24): navigating away fades the marked region out in 200ms, ease-in, faster than the 450ms appearance, so the page leaves as it came instead of being cut; forwards fill keeps it out until the next page paints, and a back-forward-cache restore clears it. Under prefers-reduced-motion it navigates at once. Update 2026-10-25: a picture with skeleton's placeholder (class ds-skeleton-image) is not held invisible: it shows its grey box while it loads and fades in by itself.
a11y_notes: Opacity and a 4px rise, 450ms; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Content stays in the accessibility tree while it fades.
